attempts.raw_response: The women, however, were more active and industrious, and it was from them that I finally obtained some dried fruits and provisions by dint of much bargaining. The principal trade of Redutkale consists in the transit of goods between Persia and the Black Sea, and the inhabitants appear to derive a comfortable livelihood from their position as carriers rather than as cultivators of the soil. The surrounding country, though capable of producing abundant harvests, lies mostly untilled, and one sees few signs of agricultural industry. The climate is mild even in winter, and the valley in which the town is situated enjoys a considerable degree of fertility where proper attention is paid to cultivation. I was informed that the roads leading to the interior are frequently infested with bandits, which renders travel both difficult and dangerous for merchants and caravans.

pair.human_continuation:
The people
are too lazy to bring wood from the forest; they work only when the
greatest necessity compels them, and require to be paid
exorbitantly.  I paid as much, if not more, for eggs, milk, and
bread as I would have done in Vienna.  It might well be said that
the people are here in the midst of plenty, and yet almost starve.

I was not better pleased by the thoughtless and meaningless
performance of religious ceremonies among these people.  On all
occasions, they cross themselves before eating or drinking, before
entering a room, before putting on an article of clothing, etc.  The
hands have nothing else to do but to make crosses.
pair.prefix:
The neighbouring people were
formerly known under the name of Huns and Alani.  The Amazons are
said to have dwelt in the country between the Caucasus and the
Caspian Sea.

The little town of Redutkale may contain about 1,500 inhabitants.
The men are so indolent that, during the five days that I passed
here, I could not procure a few grapes or figs for love or money.  I
went daily to the bazaar, and never found any for sale.

source_document.title: A Woman's Journey Round the World by Ida Pfeiffer
